chapters.text: NOVA and ADA explore a private desktop companion. The goal is conversation that connects naturally with useful software.
Speech recognition turns a spoken request into text. This animated signal illustrates that handoff; it is not a microphone recording.
Ollama runs the language model locally. Conversation context moves from the desktop application to inference and back.
The interface presents a reply and speech gives it a voice. Explicit desktop actions remain separate from ordinary conversation.
The current work is a laptop application. A physical desk companion is a future direction, not a shipped device.
BILLi and BoBA is a storefront for custom press-on nails. Product detail and mobile browsing drive the experience.
Visitors explore the collection and narrow their choices. Product pages bring the visual detail of each set into focus.
Photo-sizing guidance helps explain the order process. The design gives customers a clearer path from browsing to choosing.
Cart, checkout and order-tracking screens connect the customer journey. These panels reconstruct that flow; they are not live orders.
Supabase-backed media and admin workflows support the storefront. The live website is available separately from this visual briefing.
Sadafuli by Isha brings Indian craft into a digital storefront. The brief connects brand presentation with a practical shopping journey.
Collections and product pages guide discovery. Images, fabric information and product details help visitors understand what they are choosing.
Cart and wishlist flows keep browsing connected. The checkout view assembles the selected products into an order enquiry.
Checkout prepares an order enquiry for WhatsApp. Payment and final confirmation are handled through the store’s conversation, not this website.
Protected admin tools manage products, images and collections. Supabase supports authentication, storage and access rules behind the publishing workflow.
Sentinel connects a local camera feed to detection and monitoring. The corridor on screen is a recreated scene, not live surveillance.
YOLO checks for people while OpenCV tracks motion. The moving subject and bounding box illustrate the detection stage.
Alert-hold and stability logic address flickering states and repeated triggers. The goal is an understandable event, not a noisy stream.
Timestamped evidence snapshots connect a detection to its record. A Flask dashboard presents monitoring status and intrusion evidence.
The capture-to-dashboard workflow was validated locally. Field reliability, accuracy and response time still need formal measurement.
A new research direction: AI smart glasses. The ambition is useful assistance in everyday life, without another screen in your hand.
A proposed first-person camera captures a moment when requested. The scene shown here illustrates an idea; no camera is active.
A voice question accompanies the selected view. A companion device could prepare that context for an online multimodal model.
A spoken answer returns through the wearable. Fast interaction, practical power use and a comfortable frame are design goals to investigate.
This is a concept, separate from NOVA and Sentinel. Hardware selection and testing come next. Augmented reality remains a later possibility.
